Electronic devices in the medical field range from portable home-testing tools to complex hospital machinery. Common examples include pacemakers, digital blood pressure monitors, electrocardiogram (ECG) machines, pulse oximeters, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanners. [](https://www.allpcb.com/allelectrohub/medical-electronics-devices-and-industry-outlook)

- **ECG / EKG machines:** Record the electrical signals of the heart.

- **Ultrasound machines:** Use sound waves to image internal organs.

- **Blood glucose meters:** Measure sugar levels in small blood samples.

- **Pulse oximeters:** Clip onto a finger to check blood oxygen levels. [](https://www.codrey.com/electronics/medical-electronics-applications/)

### Monitoring Devices

- **Patient bedside monitors:**

Track heart rate, breathing, and blood pressure in real time.

- **Wearable vital-sign monitors:** Track daily heart rhythms or physical activity.

- **Continuous glucose monitors (CGMs):** Provide ongoing updates on blood sugar via tiny sensors. [](https://www.allpcb.com/allelectrohub/medical-electronics-devices-and-industry-outlook)

### Therapeutic and Life-Support Devices

- **Pacemakers:** Implanted devices that send safe electrical pulses to keep the heart beating properly.

- **Defibrillators:** Deliver an electric shock to restart or reset a dangerous heart rhythm.

- **Ventilators:** Use microcontrollers and air pressure sensors to help patients breathe.

- **Infusion pumps:** Precisely control how fast fluids or medicines go into a patient's IV. [](https://www.codrey.com/electronics/medical-electronics-applications/)
